landmarks.name: Malabo Cathedral
landmarks.writeup: A prominent Roman Catholic cathedral located in the capital city, Malabo, known for its colonial architecture.

wiki.extract: Malabo is a city in Equatorial Guinea, located in the province of Bioko Norte. It is located on the north coast of the island of Bioko. In 2018, the city had a population of approximately 297,000 inhabitants.

landmarks.name: Pico Basile
landmarks.writeup: The highest peak in Equatorial Guinea, located on Bioko Island, popular for hiking and offering panoramic views.

wiki.extract: Pico Basilé, located on the island of Bioko, is the tallest mountain of Equatorial Guinea. With an elevation of 3,011 metres, it is the summit of the largest and highest of three overlapping basaltic shield volcanoes which form the island. From the summit, Mount Cameroon can be seen to the north-east. Pico Basilé lies close to the city of Malabo. The very top is used as a broadcast transmitting station for RTVGE and microwave relay station for various communication networks.

landmarks.name: Bioko Island
landmarks.writeup: An island known for its biodiversity, volcanic landscapes, and as the location of the capital, Malabo.

wiki.extract: Bioko is an island of Equatorial Guinea. It is located 32 km (20 mi) south of the coast of Cameroon, and 160 km (99 mi) northwest of the northernmost part of mainland Equatorial Guinea. Malabo, on the north coast of the island, is the former capital city of Equatorial Guinea. Bioko's population was 335,048 at the 2015 census and it covers an area of 2,017 km2 (779 sq mi), making it the fourth largest island in Africa. The island is part of the Cameroon line of volcanoes and is located off the Cameroon coast, in the Bight of Biafra portion of the Gulf of Guinea. Its geology is volcanic; its highest peak is Pico Basile at 3,012 m (9,882 ft).

landmarks.name: Monte Alen National Park
landmarks.writeup: A protected area rich in wildlife including gorillas and chimpanzees, showcasing the country's natural heritage.

wiki.extract: Monte Alén National Park is located near the center of Equatorial Guinea. It was established in 1990. With an area of 2,000 km2 (770 sq mi), it is the country's largest national park. The goliath frog, one of the prominent amphibians found in the park, is the biggest frog in the world; hunting it is prohibited.

cultural_events.name: Fang Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional festival celebrating the Fang ethnic group's culture with music, dance, and rituals.

wiki.extract: White Fang is a 2018 animated film directed by Alexandre Espigares. Based on the 1906 book White Fang by Jack London, the film features the voices of Nick Offerman, Rashida Jones, Paul Giamatti, and Eddie Spears as natives of Alaska who, at different times, come to know White Fang, a free spirited and at times violent wolfdog who eventually bonds with Offerman's character, a gentle master named Weedon Scott. The film also features Dave Boat, Daniel Hagen, and Stephen Kramer Glickman in the original English version, and Virginie Efira, Raphaël Personnaz, and Dominique Pinon in the French dub.

cultural_events.name: Independence Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on October 12, marking the country's independence from Spain in 1968 with parades and cultural displays.

wiki.extract: Independence Day is celebrated annually on 15 August as a public holiday in India commemorating the nation's independence from the United Kingdom on 15 August 1947. On this day the Indian Independence Act 1947 came into effect, transferring legislative sovereignty to the Indian Constituent Assembly. India attained independence following the independence movement noted for largely non-violent resistance and civil disobedience led by the Indian National Congress under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi.

food_writeup: Equatorial Guinean cuisine features staples like cassava, plantains, and yams, often accompanied by fish, chicken, and spicy sauces influenced by Spanish and indigenous flavors.
brief_history: Equatorial Guinea was a Spanish colony until gaining independence in 1968. It has since been ruled by President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo since 1979. The country has significant oil reserves which have influenced its economy.
current_conflicts: No major active conflicts, but the country faces political repression and human rights concerns.

commentary.inflation_management: Equatorial Guinea's inflation has been low throughout, anchored by the Central African CFA franc's peg to the euro: it never exceeded 5.7% (2009) and troughed at -0.1% in 2021, averaging around 3%. The peg delivered price stability even as the real economy contracted for most of the 2014-2021 period. But low inflation masked a deep competitiveness problem: with oil declining and the real exchange rate rigid, the non-oil economy has withered, and monetary policy, set regionally by the BEAC, offers no tool for adjustment. Price stability here is the stability of stagnation.
commentary.debt_management: Equatorial Guinea went from virtually no debt to distress in a decade. At the 2012 oil peak the ratio was just 6.9% of GDP (0.5% in 2008, the series low), and GDP in USD terms hit $22.4bn. As oil fields declined and prices crashed in 2014, revenues collapsed while spending did not: debt climbed to 49.4% of GDP by 2020, the series high, and remains elevated at a projected 40.9% in 2025. A 2018 IMF Staff-Monitored Program pushed for transparency and arrears clearance, but progress has been slow. With oil output in structural decline, the debt path depends on spending restraint the government has historically avoided.

key_events.event: Oil production peaked; GDP hit a series high of $22.4bn; debt was just 6.9% of GDP.
Oil price crash exposed the lack of diversification; the economy entered a multi-year contraction.
IMF Staff-Monitored Program agreed, pressing for governance and oil-revenue transparency.
COVID-19 and a second oil crash pushed debt to 49.4% of GDP, the series high.
Debt remained near 40% of GDP as oil output continued its structural decline.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: The base case is managed decline: oil output keeps falling, debt stays elevated, and the CFA peg keeps inflation low while the non-oil economy stagnates. Upside would require genuine diversification or new hydrocarbon finds; downside is a fiscal crisis if spending is not cut as oil revenues fade. Uncertainty is moderate: the regime is stable and the peg credible, but the economic model is exhausted.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
